newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight fixtures emerge after earlier enquir.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight fixtures emerge after earlier enquir.

text.p: Firmer business prevailed on London's sugar freight market in contrast to the spate of fresh enquiry seen earlier in the week, shipbrokers said on Wednesday.
CSR fixed 22,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Queensland to Japan for 1/10 April and also quoted for 30/31,500 tonnes from the same origin to Kaohsiung for 10/20 April.
E D & F Man was also prominent in the day's firmer reported business.

It was said to have fixed 20,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Corinto to Casablanca plus options for the end of March and a further 16,000 tonnes in bags from Puerto Quetzal to Colombo, again with options, for 20/25 March.
Details of the rates achieved have yet to emerge.
Shipbrokers cited market talk that Man also fixed 11,500 tonnes of bulk sugar from Thailand to Japan for the end of March but this has still be to be confirmed.
Brazilian shippers SIMAB quoted for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Itajai to Lagos for the end of March and Louis Dreyfus was open for a prompt 10,000-bulk cargo from Jamaica to US Gulf/Atlantic.
Elsewhere, physical sugar brokers said they did not expect the result of Libya's recent tender to buy white sugar to emerge much before the weekend.
Earlier this week, Libya was reported to be in the market to buy at least one cargo of white sugar, most likely for nearby or May shipment.
Dockworkers at Colombia's port of Buenaventura are threatening new strike action which could begin in less than a month.

The workers are protesting against the port operators' failure to fulfill the terms of an accord hammered out in January, which ended a crippling nine-day stoppage that paralysed the export of 27,000 tonnes of sugar.
